sections.h2: Where do I find Comal County property records?
sections.html:
Go to the County Clerk at 150 N. Seguin, Suite 1037, New Braunfels, TX 78130, or call 830-221-1230. The clerk's page groups deeds under a Recording (OPR) heading that also covers land records, liens and judgments, military discharges, assumed names, a map and plat viewer and a general research request form.

The same page links an online land records search and a plat viewer with download. Under the Texas Constitution, as the page quotes it, the clerk is clerk of the County and Commissioners Courts and recorder of the county. That is why one office holds both your deed and the county's court files.

sections.h2: What are the Comal County Clerk's hours and branch offices?
sections.html:
The main office keeps public access hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday, and stays open to staff until 5:00 p.m. It stops taking walk-in visitors at 4:30 and closes daily from noon to 1:00 p.m. Two branch offices serve owners who live away from downtown New Braunfels.

  • Sattler office: 160 Oak Drive, Sattler, TX 78133, phone 830-387-7704
  • Bulverde office: 30470 Cougar Bend, Bulverde, TX 78163, phone 830-387-7620
  • County Court at Law clerks: 199 Main Plaza, 1st Floor, New Braunfels, phone 830-221-1240

Civil and probate filings with the County Court at Law have required e-filing from attorneys since January 1, 2015, according to the clerk's page. A paper packet will not work for those departments.

sections.h2: How do I record a deed with the Comal County Clerk?
sections.html:
Deliver a properly signed and acknowledged deed to the clerk's Recording department, and ask the front desk or the Quick Tips PDF on the clerk's page for current filing steps. The clerk's page keeps a fee schedule that was revised July 22, 2025, so check it before you bring payment.

Texas sets the floor. The 2023 county clerk manual lists a $5.00 first-page base fee and $4.00 per added page under Local Government Code 118.012 and 118.013, with separate records management, archive and technology fees stacked on top. It also says an instrument can be recorded only when it is acknowledged or sworn before an authorized officer or witnessed by two subscribing witnesses (Property Code 12.001(b)).

The clerk's page also links a property fraud alert page, which is worth a look for any owner who wants to watch for filings against a house.

sections.h2: What should I ask the Comal County Clerk before I file a deed?
sections.html:
Ask what the filer must show at the counter, how the instrument will be indexed, and whether the clerk wants the document in a particular order. A 2025 state law, Senate Bill 16, now requires a county clerk to ask for photo identification from anyone presenting a document for the real property records, to copy that ID, and to reject the filing if the person refuses. The law took effect September 1, 2025 and aims at deed fraud, according to a notice on a neighboring county clerk's site.

  • Bring a government photo ID that matches the person who will hand over the deed.
  • Confirm the grantee mailing address is printed on the deed.
  • Ask whether the clerk wants payment by check, and who the payee should be.
  • Keep the recording stamp, because title companies ask for the instrument number.

Call the Recording staff at 830-221-1230 to confirm the current requirements before you travel.

sections.h2: Where are Comal County foreclosure sales held?
sections.html:
On the Northeast courthouse steps of the historic Comal County Courthouse, 100 Main Plaza, New Braunfels, on the first Tuesday of each month. The county's foreclosure sales page says Commissioners Court ordered sales to follow Property Code Section 51.002, and it tells inquirers to contact the trustee named on each notice.

A notice on file does not mean the sale will happen on the next date. The trustee decides that, so a seller with a notice should speak with the trustee and a title company before listing.

sections.h2: Which office values my Comal County home?
sections.html:
The Comal Appraisal District, at 900 S. Seguin Ave., New Braunfels, TX 78130, values property and runs exemptions. Its official site is comalad.org, phone 830-625-8597, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. A look-alike search site at comalcad.org says on its own page that it is a private website paid for by sponsorships and not affiliated with any government agency, so use the district's address when you file anything.

The Texas Comptroller calendar gives May 15, or the 30th day after the notice is delivered if that is later, as the usual protest deadline. For the school district homestead exemption, the Comptroller exemptions page prints $140,000, plus $60,000 more for owners 65 or older or disabled. A buyer closing after January 1 can get the exemption for the rest of that year if the prior owner did not have it.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Comal County?
sections.html:
The county added about 100,000 residents between the 2010 census and the 2025 estimate. Census QuickFacts reports these numbers:

  • Population: 108,472 in 2010, 161,501 in 2020 and 209,166 in the July 2025 estimate, a 29.6% change from April 2020
  • Land area: 559.53 square miles, with 288.6 people per square mile in 2020
  • Housing units: 87,882 in July 2025, and 1,726 building permits in 2025
  • Owner-occupied rate: 76.6%, across 71,354 households
  • Median owner-occupied home value: $427,200 for 2020 to 2024
  • Median gross rent: $1,603; median household income: $101,889
  • Mean commute: 30.9 minutes; 20.8% of residents are 65 or older

The Comptroller's limitations page says a school tax ceiling for owners 65 or older can carry over proportionately to a new Texas homestead, which matters in a county where more than one in five residents is 65 or older.

sections.h2: Which Comal County records slow down a sale?
sections.html:
Four situations come up most often, and each leaves a trail in the records the clerk keeps:

  • An unreleased lien or judgment, listed under the clerk's Lien/Judgments service
  • A plat question for land that was split or sold in pieces, which the Plat Viewer helps answer
  • A deceased owner, which sends the file to the County Court at Law probate department
  • A trustee sale notice, which the foreclosure sales page and trustee both track

The clerk takes research requests on its General Research Request form. Ask a title company to run the full search before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: Which Comal County office handles which step of a sale?
sections.html:
Four offices cover most of a sale, and three of them have New Braunfels street addresses.

Comal County offices that touch a home sale, from the clerk, foreclosure and appraisal district pages

Deeds, liens, platsCounty Clerk150 N. Seguin, Ste. 1037, New Braunfels
Civil and probate casesCounty Court at Law Clerks199 Main Plaza, 1st Floor, New Braunfels

Keep instrument numbers, case numbers and the trustee's name in one folder, and hand copies to the title company when the sale opens.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Comal County Clerk?
faqs.a: The main office is at 150 N. Seguin, Suite 1037, New Braunfels, TX 78130, phone 830-221-1230. Branch offices are in Sattler (160 Oak Drive) and Bulverde (30470 Cougar Bend).

faqs.q: When are foreclosure sales held in Comal County?
faqs.a: On the first Tuesday of each month, on the Northeast steps of the historic courthouse at 100 Main Plaza in New Braunfels. Contact the trustee named on the notice with questions.

faqs.q: Is comalcad.org the official Comal Appraisal District website?
faqs.a: No. That site describes itself as a private website funded by sponsorships and not affiliated with any government agency. The district's official site is comalad.org, and its office is at 900 S. Seguin Ave. in New Braunfels.

faqs.q: Can I e-file probate or civil cases with the Comal County Clerk?
faqs.a: Yes, and attorneys must. The clerk's page says that since January 1, 2015 the County Court at Law civil and probate departments no longer accept paper filings from attorneys, so they go through eFileTexas.

faqs.q: What is the usual protest deadline for a Comal County appraisal?
faqs.a: May 15, or the 30th day after the notice of appraised value is delivered, whichever is later. The date printed on your own notice controls.
